events.title: St Jerome dies in Bethlehem
events.description: The scholar Jerome died in Bethlehem, where he had translated most of the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek. His Vulgate became the standard Bible of the Western Church for over a thousand years.

events.title: Parliament accepts Richard II's deposition and Henry IV's claim
events.description: Richard II's abdication was read to an assembly at Westminster, which then acclaimed Henry Bolingbroke as Henry IV. The Lancastrian usurpation sowed the seeds of the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute premieres in Vienna
events.description: Die Zauberflöte opened at the Theater auf der Wieden with Mozart conducting. It was a popular success, and he died nine weeks later at the age of 35.

events.title: Chamberlain returns from Munich promising 'peace for our time'
events.description: Neville Chamberlain landed at Heston waving the declaration signed with Hitler and later spoke of 'peace for our time'. Within six months Germany had seized the rest of Czechoslovakia.

events.title: James Dean dies in a car crash aged 24
events.description: Actor James Dean was killed when his Porsche collided with another car in California. Two of his three starring films were released after his death, making him a lasting icon of youth.
